canonical: An angle's size is the amount of turn, not the length of its arms — Angle X's real turn is 11 hour-marks and Angle Y's is 4, regardless of how they're drawn.
Adding the two real turns together: 11 + 4.

stem: Two angles share the same vertex. Angle X's arms turn through 11 hour-marks of a clock face, but are drawn very long. Angle Y's arms turn through 4 hour-marks, but are drawn very short. A student judges the two angles only by how long their arms look, ignoring the actual turn. If you add the two turns together (treating them as one after another starting from the 12), how many hour-marks of turn do Angle X and Angle Y add up to, based on their actual turns and not their arm lengths?
